lines: Pain and swelling in the right lower jaw that worsens before meals

The patient is a 46-year-old male with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hereditary Hemochromatosis with associated arthropathy, and Hypertension who presents to the Otolaryngology clinic with a 2-day history of pain and swelling in the right lower jaw that worsens before meals.
He reports similar episodes over the past 6 months, usually resolving spontaneously.
He denies fever, dysphagia, or recent dental procedures.
His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, well-controlled on metformin.
- Paternal grandfather: Hemochromatosis with liver cirrhosis

lines: Severe pain and swelling in the lower jaw for 2 days after biting hard candy
The patient with hereditary hemochromatosis, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and prior sialolithiasis presents with jaw pain.
He reports that the pain started shortly after he bit down on a hard piece of candy.
His medical history is significant for poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Paternal grandfather: Hemochromatosis with liver cirrhosis
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 3 years ago, 10 pack-year history).
His vital signs are as follows:
On examination, the patient is febrile with a temperature of 38.7°C (101.7°F).
He has difficulty speaking and appears to be drooling.
There is marked swelling and erythema of the submandibular region bilaterally, with tenderness to palpation.
